- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.10), as models tend to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < -0.30), as models fail to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Lag in price correction: if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid overshoot.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Overshoot after sharp spikes: if forecast rises >10% from prior day’s high, cap next forecast at +5% to avoid overcorrection.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment > 0.20, forecast should be 1–2% higher than historical mean; if sentiment < -0.20, forecast should be 1–2% lower.
